utterances.text: For the judges, the Sutra is a store up towards Gornji Ahmici, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So one woman was shot in the head, another woman was wounded and your father was wounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You also said that you saw soldiers up around the Sutra and that houses were burning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did these appear to be Muslim houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What did you see about these soldiers? How were they dressed, did they have any ribbons on their shoulders, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had camouflage uniforms and white arm bands, something like that. I do not know on which arm it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The woman that you said got shot in the head died. Do you know what happened to the other woman who was wounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I later found out that she also died.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You said you went back to your original house; continue on telling the story to the judges.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well. We returned to that house and there I dressed my father's wound. We did not know where to go because everything around us was on fire. . Then a woman appeared with her two children. She came down the road that went past the house where we were. We called her in because we knew her. This woman came inside the house and when she came in, she said that her husband and son were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Witness K, was this woman and her husband and her son, were they Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you and your family were all Muslims as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Continue on with the story.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were there in the house and that is where she told us this and then my father, my uncle and I decided to go and hide somewhere. We went to the garage which was above the house, it was a triple car garage which had a roof over it, so we went into the first one. We entered there and inside, there was a ditch. It was something like a storage space, and we climbed down into this ditch and there we found some kind of a can, bucket, something for storing food and he sat on it and I crouched next to him and the uncle was on the staircase that was leading down into this ditch and on the top, it was a wooden lid. On top of all of that, it was some kind of a cardboard box, flattened. There was also a little window there which let out to the -- you could see the corner of the house from it. That is where we stayed in this kind of a ditch for some 20, 30 minutes. Then we heard voices saying, "surround him" and then they said, "you are surrounded". Then there was a burst of fire. After this shooting, you could hear a few shots ringing out around the house. We could not see anything, but we heard this. After these shots, I saw through this small window as my mother was being led away, I did not see the rest of them. The soldiers remained there, I saw that they were in camouflage uniforms. Then they came out of the house carrying some things, I saw the stereo and the TV which they put by the side of the house, near that corner, and after that we heard more voices, we heard people walking around, and we felt and we saw that the house was on fire, and we heard someone say, "are we going to torch everything?". The other voice said, "no, leave it for later", that meaning the garages. They set the house on fire and walked away. I do not know exactly in which direction. Then my father, my uncle and I just stayed in this ditch that day until 17th April in the morning, until around 9.00 and then at least four soldiers appeared again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Before we move into the 17th, I believe, Mr. President, you wanted to break, as opposed to breaking at the start of the 17th -- if you want the witness to continue on the 17th we will do that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No, we are going to have a break and we will resume at 4.10. (3.50 pm) (A short break) (4.10 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The court is in session. Please show the accused in. (Accused brought in)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Go right ahead, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Witness K, I did not ask you this before, but how old were you when these events were taking place in Ahmici, on 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not fully 18, so I was still a minor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the court's permission if we could then turn to Exhibit 138? Again, there is no need to put this on the ELMO. If we could have the witness and your Honours as well as counsel look at Exhibit 138, which is an excerpt from Exhibit 50, and then have the witness identify some locations that he just discussed. May I proceed, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Go right ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Witness K, the markings on this, and the numbers, you and I have discussed together, have we not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The house that is circled with the number 1, that was the house that you were living in in Ahmici, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the dotted line that is numbered number 2 is the approximate path that you took up to the Sutra on the morning of 16th April, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And number 3 there, that is the Sutra, going up towards Gornji Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were the houses that were burning up there when you went up there, were they over to the left of the Sutra?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You said you were up there with a group of Muslims, and that would be in the area of the circle that is number 4, the oblong circle, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: By the way, the two women that were shot up in that area, were they both Muslims as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You then stated that you retraced your path from the area around number 4 and took the dotted line number 5 back to the house number 1, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Then you said you went and hid in the garage with your father and uncle. Would that be designated as number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The house that the soldiers put on fire on the 16th would be the house that you were living in, number 1, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just before we broke about 20 minutes ago, you were going to begin to tell the judges about 17th April 1993; could you do that, Witness K? What happened on the 17th, the next day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. On the 17th, around 9.00, we were in this ditch, this pit. We saw soldiers wearing camouflage uniform, that is I saw soldiers in camouflage uniforms, who were approaching these garages. I saw four of them, I do not know if there were more, I did not see any more. Then they started entering these garages. There were three of these garages, three partitions. In the first garage, it was also a storage, and the second was also a storage unit and the third one was a chicken coop of sorts. We heard soldiers' voices, "shall we torch everything?", and he said, "you do it, he was your friend". After that, we could hear voices, "did you find anything? Did you find anything?". We were in this garage, in this pit, and we could hear somebody walking around this garage. Then we smelled gasoline. It was being poured over this garage where we were. We also heard some shots and one said, "are there any chicken around?". The garages were starting to burn, and myself, my father and my uncle were in this pit. Then we hear these shots and we could not stay there any more because the garages were on fire now. So we came out of this pit into the garage which was already going up in flames, the three of us did. The soldiers who were around the house were shooting at the chicken who were running around the field. They had their backs to us, so that my father and my uncle managed to run from the garage into the house without the soldiers noticing them. As I was starting to run, one of the soldiers turned around and I went back into the garage. I could hear some strange noise around my hair, I leaned into the garage and then I ran across over into the house. My father and uncle were already in the bathroom in the house. We stayed there, there were still some shots and some voices, "take a few chicken, let us take a few and let us go", and that is what happened, they took a few and then they walked away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for a second, Witness K. You said that you heard some strange noise around your hair when you were still in the garage; what was the strange noise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I felt that my hair was on fire. It was like crackling of my hair, so I leaned against a wall of the garage, because the flames were licking upwards, and then after that, I ran across into the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You said several minutes ago that you heard the soldiers say, "should we set fire to the garage?" , and one soldier said, "you do it, it is a friend of yours". Based on that conversation, did you conclude anything about who these soldiers were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the basis of this conversation, I concluded these were local men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You said that you, your uncle and your father made it back into the main house and that would be back in the house circled with number 1. Was that house still on fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The house burned down on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What was the condition of the house when you went into it on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was all burnt out, the walls were burned, everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Take us back to the point where you are back into the house, continue to tell the judges what happened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the bathroom, we moved to another part of the house which was kind of a storage area under a staircase. That is where we moved on the 17th, under this staircase, my father, my uncle and myself. That was a bit hidden, it was like a storage area. That is where we spent the 17th and the 18th, the 19th and 20th, and on the 20th we found there in this storage area, we found a bottle with vinegar and some sugar and that is what we ate in this period. On the 21st, we heard some strange noise. We saw personnel carriers, the UN ones, which came up from the main road and stopped in front of the mosque in Ahmici. We saw some UN soldiers climbing out of these personnel carriers and as we were observing, we saw that there were three men who approached the house where we were staying. They had blue uniforms and they had gas masks on their heads. We were in this house, and one of these men entered the kitchen, the other one went upstairs and the third stayed there. We pulled back further under that staircase. They went through the house and then they came out. We thought they were UNPROFOR and we started coming out -- to come out. Father went out first and then my uncle and then myself. Father said, "people, do not be afraid, we will not do anything to you", and then one of those men in the blue uniform jumped up, he was startled, and he said, "Jesus Christ, we are looking for the dead ones and there are still some alive". The one standing next to him waved and I noticed from the house that two soldiers were running up the road, one in a camouflage uniform and one in a black uniform. Then the curses started immediately, they cursed our balija mothers and they said, "kill", but the man who said "Jesus Christ", he said, "take these men up in front of the command". So we started from there, they took us there, we had to put our hands up behind our heads and we had to look down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for a second, Witness K. Did you see any insignia on the uniform of either the soldier in the black uniform or the soldier in the camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the black uniform I only saw the name "Joker" embroidered, I do not know which arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: At this point, had you concluded that these soldiers and the men dressed in blue with the gas masks were not with UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We concluded that these men were not UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you went outside and they took you outside and you said you put your hands on your head, did you see any bodies, any dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw a body by the gate leading up to the house. It was like a skeleton, it was all burnt out, singed below the knees. It was more singed than burnt, this body, and I noticed shoes on the body's feet that were the same kind of shoes that our neighbour from number 7 owned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Witness K, you said that you recognised it by the shoes and that the body was singed. Did you think that that body had just been dumped there or that the body had been burnt there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was dumped there, because you could not see any grass that burnt around the body, and we had also heard some voices beforehand, something to the effect that this body was dumped there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Earlier, had one of these three men told you that they were looking for dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said, when he said, "Jesus Christ, we are looking for the dead ones and there are still some live ones here".

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: After you were taken out of the house and you put your hands on your head, tell the judges what happened after that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw this dead body and then they took us in the direction of Zume. We had to keep our hands up, they ordered us not to turn around or look sideways or else they would shoot us in the head. So we started up there towards Zume by the stadium and we ended up in front of a house, in front of which there was a desk and some benches, and there were five or six soldiers. Most of them wore camouflage uniforms and some wore black uniforms. I did not notice any insignia there, and immediately they started cursing our Ahmic mother, balija mother, "kill them". One of them ordered us to sit down on that bench and so my father and my uncle sat on one side and I sat across from them on another bench. There was a man sitting across from us, he was I think a Croat, an older man. He said, "kill the young one, kill the young one". Then another soldier approached in black trousers, black T-shirt, long sleeved one, he came over to me and he said -- and again this other one is saying, "kill him, kill him", and I was sitting down. He approached me and he pulled up his sleeves up to his elbows and he said, "we will see who mourns the most". I noticed that this soldier had two knives. He came over to me and he took me by the shoulder and this older man, "kill the young one". I was sitting down there and he put his hand on my shoulder, this soldier with two knives, and he said, "we will see now whose mother mourns the most", and he grabbed me by the hair and pulled my head backwards, and he had noticed that my hair was singed, and he said, "you see, you escaped but you are not going to escape the fire". A woman was there, she just looked over towards us and then entered this house in front of which we were. Then a tall man came out of it, he was 30 to 35, he had a small beard, and he asked my father whether he was such and such a person, and whether he had a disabled sister. My father replied that he was that man, and he said, "pull back from these people", and that is what happened. The soldier with two knives who stepped back turned around at one point and said that he would come for me to kill me. After that, my father asked this gentleman who had told them to leave us alone what was going to happen to us next. We were just sitting there until a truck arrived which was a refrigerator truck. Some soldiers arrived, they opened up this truck, we were ordered to climb in and so we entered the truck. We were in it and we were being taken somewhere, we did not know where. After about 20 to 30 minutes, the vehicles came to a stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for one moment, Witness K. You said that they put you in a refrigerator truck. Were you put in that truck with your father and your uncle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers put in the truck also?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were two soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What type of soldiers were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were two soldiers with regular HVO insignia in camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Where did that refrigerator truck ultimately stop after 20 to 30 minutes -- before I ask that question, is the place where you were talking about where your father was being interrogated and you were being threatened, is that number 8 on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So let us go back with the story that you were telling. Where did the truck drop you off after 20 to 30 minutes and what happened when you got there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The refrigerator truck stopped, it was opened and we were taken out. We saw that this was the school in Donje Dubravica, so we were in front of the school in Donje Dubravica. There was a group of five or six soldiers out there too and also in the hallway who were cursing our balija mothers, et cetera, swearing. They took us into the school. Then a soldier came out in a camouflage uniform who said, "bring those men over here". They took us to some kind of office, a room in that school. Three tables were put together there, and behind these three tables there were three chairs, about a metre or a metre and a half between each. Then we were ordered to sit down, to sit in those chairs so we walked in and we sat down. A soldier who was sitting at the corner of one of these tables with his feet on the table, he pointed his rifle at us. At that moment, a man walked in, dark, with a moustache, about 30 to 35. He walked into this room where we were, and then our questioning started, who we were, where were we from, where we were before that, what we were doing, what our names were. After this questioning, he introduced himself to us. He said, "I am Marinko, and I am the commander of this camp". He seemed familiar to me, I think I saw him before that. After this questioning, he said that the three of us, my father, my uncle and I, should go to the hall. We were brought to the hall, there were men and women there and children too, it was really the gym of that school. We were brought into the gym, there were women there and men and children, and we stayed there. We received only a little bit of food every 24 hours. On the 24th, UNPROFOR came, but before that, in the evening, people would be taken out to dig trenches. They did not take me because I was exhausted. My uncle was taken out to dig trenches. On 24th, UNPROFOR came and they registered us, and we were given cards. That day, my father was taken away by UNPROFOR because he was wounded. UNPROFOR took him away, but I did not know where he was taken to. My uncle and I stayed on in the camp. On the 25th or 26th, I am not too sure what day it was, a girl who was about 20 years old, I did not know her before that, I was lying on the floor on a blanket, she came up to me and she sat next to me and she was crying. I asked her, "why are you crying?", and then she cried even more. I said, "why are you crying?", and she said, "I was taken away last night". I said, "who took you away?"; "I was taken away by some soldiers", and I said, "what happened?"; "I was raped"; "do you know how many of them and who they were?"; "I do not know", she said, "because I had fainted". That is where we were, that is where we spent our days, in confinement, until 1st May. On 1st May, UNPROFOR came again and they announced to us that there would be an exchange, that we would be exchanged. We were told that we could choose whether we would go to Zenica or to Travnik, that we should register accordingly. My uncle and I decided to go to Travnik, and on 1st May, around 3.00 or 4.00, UNPROFOR came with a bus. Before that, they took away the people who were imprisoned there with me, they took them to Zenica and my uncle and I, there were 22 of us altogether, we were taken to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness K. If there is no further clarification, maybe you could answer some additional questions from the counsel of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. When you got to Dubravica school, you said that the -- were the soldiers in the Dubravica school in camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you see any insignia on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see any insignia, but it was being said that they were the Vitezovi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your uncle was taken to dig trenches. Do you know where he dug trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He told me that he went to Sivrino Selo, to Dubravica and around there, that is where he dug those trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you in the gym when they came and took people out to dig the trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did this go on almost every night when you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just going back to clarify a point that you said at the beginning of your testimony, you said that in March you moved to Ahmici. Had you moved from Nadioci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was this as a result of some problems with or harassment by HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know the names of those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Nadioci, I know that it was Cicko and Rutko who harassed me, these are their nicknames.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: After this, did you learn what Cicko's name was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cicko's name is Miroslav. I do not know his last name exactly, but Miroslav is his first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness K. Mr. President and your Honours, I just would offer into evidence at this time Exhibit 138 and I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, no objection. Turning to the counsel for the Defence, two lawyers for the Defence, Mr. Nobilo, go right ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to put a question or two in connection with the house where they lived, so perhaps it would be a good thing to exclude the public from this part of the hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. For the duration of these few questions, could we go into a private session, Registrar, please? (In private session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (In open session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Now we are back in the public session, so please go ahead, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness K, you mentioned the trouble you had in Nadioci. Could you tell me before we move on to this trouble, who was Cicko? What was he well known for and what do you know about him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know Cicko, not all that well, I know that his name is Miroslav, his first name, and that he provoked me before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is he well known for killing a Muslim and for blowing up his bed with explosive, yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did he blow up his entire house or only the bed and the body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not walk up to the house, I heard it, I did not see it. My father went to this man's funeral and he said that the house was blown up too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you present when the police came from Vitez for the inquest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you hear that the police had come?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that the police had come, but I was not present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you hear about Cicko finishing up in jail?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard something, but after that, three or four days after that, I saw Cicko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Tell me, what did Cicko do to you exactly, briefly in two or three sentences, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cicko; he held a rifle pointed at me and he said he would kill me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Where was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Nadioci.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the house where you lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In another house where I was staying at present, at a party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What was he seeking there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know why he was there, he was looking for weapons in that house, so they walked into the house, violently, they were searching the place and he was carrying a rifle, a Karabin, and he turned it to me and said he would kill me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were they looking for money or for people's valuables?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were they drunk, the two of them, on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cicko was not, and you could feel the smell of alcohol from Rutko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Later on, did you meet Cicko again and did you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him at my place where he wanted to apologise to me, that very same night when that had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Tell me, when you went to the place called Sutra, the place that you referred to with those women, did you come to that deep ditch or had you crossed it before that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We came to this deep ditch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But you did not cross it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Are there any bushes or any trees or forest there by the deep ditch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Tell me now, when you were walking, from what side did the bullets, the firing come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly from what direction because they were firing from all sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You did not see who was shooting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I could not see it exactly. I had seen some soldiers by Sutra who were running from one house to another, but I did not see who was actually doing the shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: At that time, was there a lot of infantry fire in Ahmici and in the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not at that point in time. There was not a lot of firing, you could hear some shooting but it was not that strong.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You heard some shooting from Sutra?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I do not know the people who were hit, whether they were hit from that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Tell me, when they were hit, which way were they facing, the direction in which you were moving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Depending on where who stood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But they were hit in the front, not in the back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the front, and my father was hit on the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were these individual shots or were these bursts of gunfire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bursts of gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So we have understood that you did not see who actually did the shooting. Tell me, when you were already arrested, and when this old man kept saying, "kill him, kill him", did he say something else? Did he mention, for example, the following words? I will tell you what your previous statement says on page 7: "Kill him, kill him in front of the house, he is responsible for the death of three of our men", or something like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he kept saying, "kill the kid, kill the kid, he is responsible for the death of three of their people, three of their soldiers".

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Could you describe the man who practically saved you at the intervention of that woman, who said that you should be left alone? What did he look like, could you describe him in detail?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was fair, blonde, about 1 metre 80 centimetres, tall. He had a small beard, he was in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did he look like a commander to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did look like a commander to me, because other people were asking him what to do too, because he was the one who said we should be left alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you see him before that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him when I would pass by Pican's house. He was in front of it, sometimes. I did not know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So we can conclude that he was practically a neighbour, that he lived somewhere round there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him there a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you were put in the refrigerator truck, was it on, the cooling, or was it off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you arrived in Dubravica, was any mention made of Croat Muslim units, when people talked to your father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you tell us in a few sentences what all that was about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was about the following: there was some interrogating by Marinko, who did what and how. I was wearing boots on my feet, Nihad Skrobo gave me these boots as a present, and he asked me about them and he said, how did I get those boots, usually anybody could have them, and I answered that Nihad Skrobo had given them to me and he said that he knew Nihad Skrobo and that he was in Croatia together with him at the front-line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Tell me, your father, was he a member of the BH-Army at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, he was. That was the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What unit did he belong to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly. I know that it was called the Territorial Defence, I do not know what unit it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence in Ahmici or another Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he would go out to Turbe, my father, against the Chetniks. Seven days before all of these events, he was together with the Croats at the front-line against the Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Tell me, what are you doing now, where do you live? You do not have to tell me exactly where you live, but what do you do now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I object, your Honour. I object to the question as to what his current employment is on an open record.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In the most general terms, he does not have to say anything specific. Very generally, what is he doing with his life now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be careful, Mr. Nobilo. Just please be cautious. Do you want to add something, Mr. Kehoe? We will check the transcript, that is what we will do, because we may commit some errors, so we do have to be very careful. The witness has to be careful. Witness K, it is in your interest to be taking protective measures for you. If you think that in a reply you are -- yes, I know. (Pause). Let me sum up. As Judge Riad pointed out, there are some real concerns. The protection of the witness is the task of all parties, the judges, Defence and Prosecution and for you as well, Witness K. If there is a question you are uncomfortable with, Witness K, you should say so, you should say, "no, I would rather not answer that. That would give away my identity", because this is a public session. You are protected but this is a public session, as my fellow judges have just pointed out to me. That said, we will check in the transcript of the hearing which subsequently is published, so the Registrar will see to it that that is deleted so please keep it simple, Witness K, and if you think that a given question is not in the interests of your safety, just say so. Thank you, gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness did not answer anything. I just asked him what he was doing now, and then the objection was raised, so we did not make any kind of mistake, so there is nothing in the transcript that should not be there. I simply wondered whether he was working or going to school et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think if the question is whether he is working or going to school and the witness can say he is working --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Wait a minute, Mr. Hayman is not hearing anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I did not have a translation of your Honour's comment. That was what I was concerned about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It was a shame. It was a very good comment. No, I think we can leave it at that. The incident is over and done with, the witness did not say anything and there is nothing to fear. Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I have no further questions. That was my last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe is already standing so maybe wants to pick up on just a few items. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just a few, Mr. President. You mentioned in response to

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: for blowing this Muslim up in his house, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Four days later, you saw him back out on the street, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Also, in questions by Mr. Nobilo, he read your statement, and he said that this old man said that you were responsible for the death of three of their soldiers; do you recall those questions by him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he said, "kill the young one", as if I had killed those three.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Had you killed anybody?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not, we did not even have anything, we did not have anything to kill them with.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What did your father say at the time when you were being accused of killing these three soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He got up and he said, "we did not kill anyone, we had nothing to kill people with and we would not have killed them".

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Defence asked you some questions on cross-examination about these Croat Muslim units; do you recall those questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Your father talked to Marinko about those units, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Those units were units from the outbreak at the beginning of the war in 1992, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When this happened, there were no Croat Muslim units, were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe, for being so brief. I am going to turn to my fellow judges. Judge Riad?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I will call you Witness K. Good afternoon. I would like to have some clarifications: when you were leaving Sutra, you saw what you call soldiers running from house to house around Sutra and apparently putting fire in the houses, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What made you think they are soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I saw as they were running across one house was already starting to burn and I saw the camouflage uniforms on the soldiers who were running from one house to the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What kind of camouflage uniform was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Regular camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Of HVO, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well yes, as far as I know, to my knowledge they were the HVO uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When these people came in on the 19th to the storage area where you were, you thought they were UNPROFOR people, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Then they were not in camouflage uniform at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not fully understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You remember you said on the 19th you were in the storage area and you thought that the people who came in were UNPROFOR people and you went to them, you came out of your hiding and you went to them. Did I understand you rightly? Then you discovered that they were not UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we discovered that they were not UNPROFOR, they were wearing blue uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Were they disguised as UNPROFOR or was it also the HVO normal dress?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The regular blue uniform was for the members of the civilian protection, they wore such uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What do you call "civilian protection"? UNPROFOR or Croat or Bosnian? What was the civilian protection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I put it differently. Were there any Croat troops assuming civilian protection, protecting people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You always spoke of those who took you around as soldiers. For instance, you said that a soldier with two knives came to you and said, "whose mother will mourn the most?". Also, why do you think he is a soldier? Then there was Marinko, who you said was a commander. Did they look like regular army soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The one in black uniform had black boots, black trousers, black sweat shirt and two knives and he looked to me like a soldier. Marinko had a camouflage uniform and he looked like a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And the man who saved you, did he look like a soldier too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was in a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did he look like a commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Then you noticed that the commander's orders are being obeyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You spoke of the young girl of 20 years old who cried and told you she had been raped. Did she tell you she had been raped by soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Riad. Judge Shahabuddeen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Let us go back to this incident when you thought that some UNPROFOR personnel were approaching, and you came out and discovered that that was not correct; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I have a recollection that you described one of the men as being in a black uniform and being a Joker, am I correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The other soldier or soldiers were in camouflage, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you hear them all talking to one another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were arrested, we did not hear their conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I know that you may not remember exactly what they said, what I am asking is whether you heard any of them talking to the others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He only said -- the one in the blue uniform just said that we should be taken in front of the command, so these two who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: He was talking to the other two soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: To whom was he talking then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He just said -- he said to those two soldiers, "take them up in front of the command post".

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That is the Joker soldier told the two who were in camouflage to take them up to the command post, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the one in the blue uniform, man in the blue uniform said to these two, one had a black Joker uniform and the other soldier had a camouflage uniform, he told the two of them to take me and my father and my uncle to the command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So you had the impression that the three of them were acting together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us go to the incident during which someone threatened you with a knife, threatened to slit your throat, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was the man standing next to me with two knives and he said that he was going to kill me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You remember that Mr. Marinko, I think, intervened and saved you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: He was a Croat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did anyone tell Marinko of this allegation that you had killed some Croat soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Marinko did not ask us that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I am not asking you whether Marinko asked such a question; what I am asking is whether anyone told Marinko of that allegation, that you had killed some Croat soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness K. That is the end of your testimony. So we have taken protective measures, you have nothing to fear. The Tribunal would like to thank you. Now we are going to bring down the blinds again, so that you will be safe to the end, so that no one can see you, so please remain seated for the time being. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, just a question I forgot to put this to you. This witness had been forecast to last how long, about? I do not remember what the expectations were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I simply do not recall, your Honour. I believe it was two hours or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. Who is going to be introducing the next witness, Mr. Kehoe, Mr. Harmon? There is no other witness? No more witnesses. We are going too fast, if I have got it right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Neither me nor Mr. Harmon will introduce the next witness today. We do not have any other witness for today, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Okay, fine. Do you know we are not sitting tomorrow morning because there is a plenary with other judges? Tomorrow afternoon, do you have witnesses ready for tomorrow, in other words some problems, Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, we anticipate the arrival of several witnesses late this evening and we will do our best to prepare a witness or two witnesses for the time available tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You need not prepare them, because since you have the presiding judge who is doing all the groundwork for you, it should make it all a lot easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. President. I have a personal announcement to make to the court. As a result of professional and personal commitments, I will be absent from the Tribunal and in the United Kingdom probably until after the December break. I will be replaced by a very experienced American Prosecutor, Nancy Paterson, who will be assisting Mr. Harmon and Mr. Kehoe in my absence. I apologise to the court and to my learned friends opposite for having to do this, but it is unavoidable, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Does this mean that you will then be coming back in January, Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Perhaps sooner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Good, we are delighted to hear it. Of course we are looking forward to working with Ms. Paterson. Now we can leave it at that. We will be in court tomorrow at 3.00 pm, is that right? (Pause). All right then, we will resume tomorrow at 3.00 pm. (5.25 pm)

procedural_notes.text: cross-examination by Mr. Nobilo that Cicko was arrested
(Hearing adjourned until 3.00 pm the following day)
